feedback:
Earlier evidence: iteration 1 (base_speed 1.2, kp 4, ki 0.2, kd 0.6, sensors at y 0.05 with x within ±0.03 and 12 mm footprints, wheel_track 0.12, mass 0.6) finished 13 of 20 oval trials at mean finish time 1.73 s, with progress 0.94 and max_error 0.045. All 20 s-bend and 20 slalom trials ended off track at progress 0.11 to 0.22, with max_error 0.063 to 0.064 against the 0.06 m limit. Line_loss_events were 1.75 on the s-bend and 1.15 on the slalom, and steering_oscillation stayed at 0.15 to 0.30. The failures are therefore on sharp bends where the tape leaves the array, not from jitter. Iteration 1 remains the best raced candidate (score 289.04).

The candidate follows that evidence. It widens the sensor footprint to 16 mm and the x spread to ±0.04 to keep the tape in view further out, lowers wheel_track to 0.10 for a faster turn rate, lowers base_speed to 1.0 to leave time to correct, and raises kp to 5 with kd 0.8 to damp it. The oval finish time of 1.73 s at speed 1.2 leaves room for a slower run and still allows completion under 3 s. Mass 0.6 and body_width 0.18 are kept, as they were in the best raced design. Nothing is obviously out of range or broken.

The risk is that five groups of fields change together, so the cause of any result will be hard to separate. Approve it so the race isolates the sensor and turn-rate changes on the sharp bends. After the race, read the results in this order. If line_loss_events fall on the s-bend and slalom but progress stays below 0.5, the array change worked and the limit is speed or gain. If steering_oscillation rises above 0.5, kp 5 is too high, so drop it toward 4. If the oval no longer completes, restore base_speed toward 1.2 while keeping the narrower track.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events drop on s-bend and slalom but progress stays below 0.5: keep the sensor change (sensor_size 0.016, x ±0.04) and raise base_speed in 0.1 steps (1.1, then 1.2), since iteration 1 finished 13 of 20 oval trials at speed 1.2 with finish time 1.73 s.

If steering_oscillation exceeds 0.5 on any track: reduce kp from 5.0 to about 4.0 and keep kd at 0.8, because iteration 1 showed oscillation of 0.30 at kp 4 with kd 0.6, and the turn gain has been raised here.
If the oval stops completing and max_error stays near 0.06 on the s-bend: revert wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.12, keeping the wider array, to isolate whether the faster turn rate is causing the drift.
